title: OpenSky State Vector Failure Rate
dataSources: ADS-B aircraft snapshots (`adsb:aircraft`), personal flight logbook (`flight:log`), commute trips (`commute:trip`), transit arrivals (`transit:arrival`), geofence events (`geofence:event`), travel documents (`travel:document`), fare quotes (`airprice:quote`).
app: Home ADS-B receiver (dump1090/readsb/tar1090 JSON feed), personal flight logbook exports, commute/transit APIs, and phone geofence webhooks via Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=opensky:state
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(vector_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by icao24
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often OpenSky state vector records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each aircraft.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize vector_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per aircraft.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It estimates which parts of your OpenSky state vector data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
